patterns_data.pattern_details: CT PPO acute hospital spend is dominated by authorization-required inpatient activity at Yale New Haven Hospital. This is a combined utilization and reimbursement problem, not just a broad market trend.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A large share of the increase sits with one hospital, creating immediate leverage for focused UM and contracting action.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Launch a joint UM and contract review for Yale New Haven Hospital PPO inpatient cases, focusing on authorization-required admissions, level of care, and reimbursement for craniotomy and sepsis episodes.
evidence_summary: About +$12.8M of the +$14.5M increase sits at YALE NEW HAVEN HOSPITAL.
Admissions increased by 150 and paid per admit rose by about $17.4K.
Craniotomy cases added about +$1.3M on 14 more admissions, with roughly +$92.7K per admit.
Sepsis cases added about +$350K on 16 more admissions.

patterns_data.why_it_matters: These episodes can evade broad trend management and require case-level clinical, discharge, and reimbursement action.

patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Rare catastrophic IP Med/Surg episodes across CT, IN, TX, and UNATTRIBUTED
key_driver_codes: Liver Transplant with MCC or Intestinal Transplant
Spinal Fusion Except Cervical with Spinal Curvature, Malignancy, Infection or Extensive Fusions with CC

patterns_data.pattern_details: A separate layer of spend comes from very rare catastrophic IP Med/Surg cases, including transplant, complex spinal fusion, cardiac surgery, and inpatient immunotherapy. These are low-frequency but very expensive episodes, often with six-figure per-admit increases. The right response is case validation and large-case management, not broad utilization policy.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A few catastrophic cases can distort market trends and require different financial and clinical controls than routine inpatient growth.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Send the identified catastrophic episodes for case-level clinical validation and large-case financial review, including contract terms for transplant, spinal fusion, and inpatient immunotherapy.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The pattern is driven by small-number, low-baseline cases, including unattributed findings, so case-level validation is needed before broader action.
evidence_summary: This pattern contributed about +$8.4M from 19 high-cost IP Med/Surg findings.
Two complex spinal fusion findings alone added about +$3.4M on 8 more admissions.
A CAR-T and immunotherapy case at YALE NEW HAVEN HOSPITAL added about +$1.3M on just 2 admissions.
Most findings are flagged as small-number or low-baseline cases.

patterns_data.pattern_details: Before acting on some authorization and provider mix signals, validate whether claims moved between authorization categories or landed in unmapped facility buckets. Auth-code redistribution is material in ME, CA, GA, and TX, and additional spend is sitting in "Not Mapped" facility classifications in KY, CT, and VA. These are gating data issues because they can mimic real utilization or rate changes.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Acting on misclassified authorization or facility data can send UM and contracting teams to the wrong problem.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Reconcile PA-required coding and facility-type mapping for the affected states, then rerun the impacted market reviews before changing UM or network strategy.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The source groups are explicitly flagged as requiring validation before action because authorization coding shifted or facility classifications are unmapped.
evidence_summary: Auth-code redistribution shows about -$2.5M in ME, +$1.8M in CA, and +$0.6M across GA and TX.
"Not Mapped" facility classifications add about +$808K in KY, +$133K in CT, and +$48K in VA.
The largest auth-code movement is CA craniotomy at about +$1.7M.
All source groups are flagged for validation before action.

patterns_data.pattern_details: Outside the largest single-state markets, the same acute-hospital pattern repeats: admissions are up, and a meaningful share of the increase is concentrated in a small provider set and a few recurring episodes. MEMORIAL HOSPITAL and ELKHART GENERAL HOSPITAL recur in Indiana, while craniotomy, aftercare, and sepsis spikes appear across several HMO acute-hospital markets. This is a provider mix pattern that should be handled through targeted hospital action rather than broad product-wide changes.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Recurring concentration creates leverage for focused provider and UM interventions across multiple markets.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Build a cross-market action list for MEMORIAL HOSPITAL, ELKHART GENERAL HOSPITAL, and the recurring sepsis and craniotomy episodes, then align network and UM interventions at the facility level.
evidence_summary: These recurring acute-hospital groups sum to about +$6.1M.
MEMORIAL HOSPITAL in IN contributed about +$838K under HMO, and ELKHART GENERAL HOSPITAL added about +$541K across HMO and POS volume-led findings.
GA and CO HMO acute-hospital craniotomy added about +$2.7M combined.
TX and NV sepsis episodes added about +$627K within the broader multi-state acute-hospital pattern.

patterns_data.pattern_details: TX has a distinct sepsis pattern inside IP Med/Surg. Most of the increase is volume-led, with much higher admissions in unspecified and E. coli sepsis, while a smaller subset of MRSA sepsis and bacteremia also carries higher intensity. This needs clinical and UM review of sepsis admissions, not a general hospital pricing response.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Sepsis utilization can scale quickly and drive avoidable inpatient spend if unmanaged.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Send TX sepsis cases to clinical and UM operations for admission-criteria, level-of-care, and care-pathway review, especially unspecified organism and E. coli cases.
evidence_summary: TX sepsis-related clinical groups total about +$1.8M.
Unspecified sepsis added about +$1.1M on 94 more admissions even though paid per admit fell by about $2.7K.
E. coli sepsis added about +$299K on 18 more admissions.
MRSA sepsis and bacteremia added another about +$409K with higher per-admit intensity on 12 more admissions.
